column2: On the authority of Abū Ḥamzah Anas ibn Mālik (may Allah be pleased with him), the servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.” Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

Lā yuʾminu (“does not truly believe”): [with] complete faith. Li-akhīhi (“for his brother”): in Islam. Mā (“what”): in the sense of “everything”. “He loves for himself”: of good, and he dislikes for him the evil that he dislikes for himself. Yuḥibbu (“loves”): love is affection.
Part of the perfection of a servant's faith is that he loves for his Muslim brother what he loves for himself.
He should dislike for his Muslim brother the evil that he dislikes for himself.
A person should guide his brothers to what benefits them and warn them against what harms them.

This hadith guides us to the fact that a believer of complete faith should love for his Muslim brother what he loves for himself. The meaning of this love is that he shares with his brother, as he would himself, in all matters of benefit, religious or worldly, such as sincere advice, guiding to good, commanding what is right

and forbidding what is wrong, and other things he desires for himself: he guides his brother to it; and whatever he dislikes, in which there is deficiency or harm, he keeps it away from him, by his words, his deeds or his wealth. This is the love intended in the hadith, not natural human love such as a father's love for his child and his wealth.
Never lose interest in a kindness you have begun; / everyone will be repaid for what he has done.
Praise keeps alive the memory of its owner, / as rain revives with its moisture the plain and the mountain.
By your life, the days are only on loan; / so take provision of their kindness as much as you can.
